title: 502. The Roman Conquest of Britain: To the Ends of the Earth (Part 4)

sentences.en: We, the most distant of peoples who dwell upon this earth, the last of the three,
sentences.zh: 我们，这片大地上最遥远的子民，三族中的最后一人，

sentences.en: have been shielded until today by our very remoteness and by the obscurity in which it has shrouded our name.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，都因我们的偏远和那笼罩着我们名号的默默无闻而受到庇护。

sentences.en: But now, the most northerly reaches of Britain lie open to our foe, and what men know nothing about is invariably a cause of fascination.
sentences.zh: 但现在，不列颠最北端的疆域已向我们的敌人敞开，而人们一无所知的事物，总是令人着迷。

sentences.en: There are no peoples who dwell beyond us, nothing but waves and rocks, and the Romans who are more terrible still,
sentences.zh: 在我们之外再无其他民族，除了波涛与岩石，还有那更可怕的罗马人，

sentences.en: for there is no escaping their exactions by submitting to them and bowing their neck.
sentences.zh: 因为向他们屈服、低头，也无法逃脱他们的勒索。

sentences.en: Men who have stripped the entire world bare, they have exhausted the dry land by plundering all it has to offer, so now they ransack the sea.
sentences.zh: 这些人剥光了整个世界，在掠夺了陆地上的一切资源后，现在又开始洗劫海洋。

sentences.en: A wealthy enemy excites their rapacity, a poor one their hunger for power.
sentences.zh: 富有的敌人激起他们的贪婪，贫穷的敌人则激起他们对权力的渴望。

sentences.en: The East and West alike have failed to satisfy their appetites.
sentences.zh: 东方和西方都无法满足他们的胃口。

sentences.en: Alone among men, they lust equally after the rich and the poor.
sentences.zh: 在人类之中，唯有他们对富人和穷人同样贪婪。

sentences.en: What they speciously call empire is merely robbery, slaughter, and looting.
sentences.zh: 他们虚伪地称之为帝国的东西，不过是抢劫、屠杀和掠夺。

sentences.en: They create a wilderness, and they call it peace.
sentences.zh: 他们制造了一片荒野，却称之为和平。

sentences.en: So that, Tom, was Mel Gibson in AD 83.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，那是公元83年的梅尔·吉布森。

sentences.en: It was, in fact, Calgicus, a British warlord who, like Mel Gibson, celebrated both for his breeding and for his valour.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那是卡尔加库斯，一位不列颠军阀，他和梅尔·吉布森一样，以其出身和英勇而闻名。

sentences.en: And he delivered that speech, didn't he, Calgicus, if he did deliver it, as we will discover, on a mountain called Gropius in the highlands of Scotland,
sentences.zh: 他发表了那篇演讲，不是吗？卡尔加库斯，如果他确实发表过的话——正如我们将要发现的那样——是在苏格兰高地一座名为格罗皮乌斯的山上，

sentences.en: or what was then called to the Romans Caledonia.
sentences.zh: 或者当时罗马人称之为喀里多尼亚的地方。

sentences.en: So we had Boudicca last time, and we were talking about how she was the first real great rich character in British history.
sentences.zh: 上次我们讲到了布狄卡，谈论了她如何成为不列颠历史上第一个真正伟大且富有传奇色彩的人物。

sentences.en: And here we have the first person in all Scottish history, don't we?
sentences.zh: 而在这里，我们见到了整个苏格兰历史上的第一人，不是吗？

sentences.en: To have a name, yeah.
sentences.zh: 一个有名有姓的人，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was very Mel Gibson, because the situation is quite Braveheart.
sentences.zh: 这非常有梅尔·吉布森的风格，因为局势简直就是《勇敢的心》。

sentences.en: So the Caledonians are on the slopes of this mountain called Gropius, and as on so many occasions in subsequent Scottish history, they're resisting a vast invasion from the south.
sentences.zh: 喀里多尼亚人驻扎在名为格罗皮乌斯的山坡上，正如苏格兰历史上随后的许多次一样，他们正在抵御来自南方的巨大入侵。

sentences.en: And it's been 40 years since the Romans landed in Kent, and they have now reached the highlands.
sentences.zh: 罗马人登陆肯特郡已经40年了，现在他们终于抵达了高地。

sentences.en: And the process of conquest, as we were discussing last time in the end of our episode on Boudicca, have been devastating.
sentences.zh: 而正如我们上次在布狄卡那一集的结尾所讨论的那样，征服的过程是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: So we said that in that great battle, perhaps 40,000 were slaughtered in the battle that ends her revolt.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，在那场伟大的战役中，在终结她起义的那场战斗里，或许有4万人被屠杀。

sentences.en: We've had genocidal campaigning in Wales, hundreds of thousands killed, hundreds of thousands enslaved.
sentences.zh: 我们在威尔士经历了种族灭绝式的战役，数十万人被杀，数十万人被奴役。

sentences.en: So you can see where Calcicus is coming from.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以理解卡尔加库斯的立场。

sentences.en: And the line with which he ends that speech, they create a wilderness and they call it peace, is probably one of the most famous denunciations of imperialism of all time.
sentences.zh: 他演讲结尾的那句“他们制造了一片荒野，却称之为和平”，大概是有史以来对帝国主义最著名的谴责之一。

sentences.en: I mean, it's often, often quoted, often repeated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它经常被引用，经常被重复。

sentences.en: And it seems to offer a counterpoint to the glory that was Rome.
sentences.zh: 它似乎为“罗马的荣耀”提供了一个反衬。

sentences.en: It seems to give us the view from the barbarian side, except that, of course, it's not actually verbatim.
sentences.zh: 它似乎给了我们一个来自蛮族视角的观点，当然，这并不是逐字记录。

sentences.en: It's essentially invented by Tacitus, the great Roman historian, who is, and this is absolutely on trend with what Roman historians do.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是由伟大的罗马历史学家塔西佗虚构的，而且这完全符合罗马历史学家的惯例。

sentences.en: There's nothing, you know, no one would see it as being poor form.
sentences.zh: 没什么大不了的，你知道，没人会觉得这有什么不妥。

sentences.en: It's absolutely expected.
sentences.zh: 这是完全在预料之中的。

sentences.en: But he is putting words into this Caledonian leader's mouth.
sentences.zh: 但他确实是把话塞进了这位喀里多尼亚领袖的嘴里。

sentences.en: And it appears in the biography of Agricola, who is the governor of Britain, who is leading the legions, say the Roman side, at the Battle of Mount Graupius.
sentences.zh: 这段话出现在《阿古利可拉传》中，阿古利可拉是不列颠的总督，也是格劳庇乌山战役中罗马军队的统帅。

sentences.en: And when Tacitus gives these words to Calcicus, it's not total fantasy.
sentences.zh: 当塔西佗把这些话赋予卡尔加库斯时，这并非完全是幻想。

sentences.en: He is very well informed on British affairs.
sentences.zh: 他对不列颠的事务非常了解。

sentences.en: Agricola was his father-in-law.
sentences.zh: 阿古利可拉是他的岳父。

sentences.en: He may well have served in Britain himself.
sentences.zh: 他本人很可能也在不列颠服过役。

sentences.en: So, to quote Anthony Burley, who's a very distinguished expert on Northern Britain in the Roman period.
sentences.zh: 所以，引用安东尼·伯利的话，他是罗马时期北不列颠非常杰出的专家。

sentences.en: And he says, why not suppose that Tacitus served in Britain in one of the four legions in the army of his father-in-law?
sentences.zh: 他说，为什么不假设塔西佗曾在其岳父军队的四个军团之一中在不列颠服役呢？

sentences.en: He could well have stayed there for two to three years.
sentences.zh: 他很可能在那里待了两到三年。

sentences.en: And he points out that in the account of Agricola's governorship that Tacitus writes, the first three years are done in great detail.
sentences.zh: 他指出，在塔西佗撰写的阿古利可拉总督任期记录中，前三年写得非常详细。

sentences.en: And then it becomes slightly more sketchy, implying that perhaps Tacitus was actually present in Britain.
sentences.zh: 然后变得稍微简略了一些，这意味着塔西佗可能确实在不列颠。

sentences.en: So, he would have had a good idea of what the Roman conquest meant for the Britons.
sentences.zh: 所以，他应该很清楚罗马的征服对不列颠人意味着什么。

sentences.en: But having said that, I think that Calcicus' speech actually tells us less about British attitudes to Roman imperialism than about Tacitus' own.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，我认为卡尔加库斯的演讲与其说是反映了不列颠人对罗马帝国主义的态度，不如说是反映了塔西佗自己的态度。

sentences.en: And it's obvious.
sentences.zh: 这是显而易见的。

sentences.en: I mean, no man who is capable of composing that speech that you read out can possibly be reckoned to view empire and conquest as an unambiguous good.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何能写出你刚才读的那段演讲的人，都不可能认为帝国和征服是绝对的好事。

sentences.en: So, the question then is, does this mean basically he's woke?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，这是否意味着他本质上是个“觉醒派”？

sentences.en: Is he a woke historian, Roman historian, part of the woke mind virus?
sentences.zh: 他是一位觉醒派历史学家，罗马历史学家，属于“觉醒思想病毒”的一员吗？

sentences.en: So, we will see.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们将拭目以待。

sentences.en: We will see.
sentences.zh: 我们将拭目以待。

sentences.en: Over the course of this episode, where Tacitus is coming from.
sentences.zh: 在本集的过程中，我们将探讨塔西佗的立场。

sentences.en: Isn't that interesting?
sentences.zh: 这难道不有趣吗？

sentences.en: The idea that the germ of the criticism of Roman imperialism, and indeed of imperialism more generally, is right there at the beginning within Roman culture itself.
sentences.zh: 这种对罗马帝国主义，乃至更广泛的帝国主义的批评萌芽，从一开始就存在于罗马文化本身之中。

sentences.en: The question is, are the reasons that Tacitus is criticising imperialism the reasons that we today might criticise imperialism?
sentences.zh: 问题是，塔西佗批评帝国主义的原因，是否就是我们今天批评帝国主义的原因？

sentences.en: And that's something that we can explore over the course of this episode.
sentences.zh: 这是我们可以在本集过程中探讨的内容。

sentences.en: So, let's get into the British context.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们进入不列颠的背景。

sentences.en: So, what is it?
sentences.zh: 那么，情况是怎样的？

sentences.en: A generation has gone by since the arrival of the Romans in southern Britain.
sentences.zh: 自从罗马人抵达不列颠南部以来，已经过去了一代人。

sentences.en: So, that speech is AD 83.
sentences.zh: 那场演讲是在公元83年。

sentences.en: We've had Boudicca's revolt.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了布狄卡的起义。

sentences.en: And after that, the sheer punitiveness, the bloodthirstiness of the Roman response to that, the destruction of the great mass of people, the horde that followed Boudicca,
sentences.zh: 在那之后，罗马人对此反应的纯粹惩罚性和嗜血程度，对跟随布狄卡的大批民众的毁灭，

sentences.en: that sends a very clear signal that the Romans are here for good.
sentences.zh: 这发出了一个非常明确的信号：罗马人是来长住的。

sentences.en: They're not going to withdraw.
sentences.zh: 他们不会撤退。

sentences.en: There was that thing that you pointed out last time, that the guy who pushed the repression was later recalled, and people felt he'd gone too far.
sentences.zh: 你上次指出的那件事，那个推动镇压的人后来被召回了，人们觉得他做得太过分了。

sentences.en: So, how did the Romans view Britain?
sentences.zh: 那么，罗马人是如何看待不列颠的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, Tacitus is not alone, I think, in feeling that the early decades of the Roman occupation
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为塔西佗并非唯一一个觉得罗马占领的最初几十年

sentences.en: have been pretty badly mismanaged, and that Boudicca's revolt is an expression of that.
sentences.zh: 管理得相当糟糕，而布狄卡的起义正是这种情绪的表达。

sentences.en: And the aftermath of Boudicca's revolt is, firstly, it's now impossible for the Romans even to contemplate withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 而布狄卡起义后的后果是，首先，罗马人现在甚至不可能考虑撤退。

sentences.en: Too much blood has been loSt.
sentences.zh: 流了太多的血。

sentences.en: Too much gold has been invested.
sentences.zh: 投入了太多的黄金。

sentences.en: It would be too great a humiliation.
sentences.zh: 那将是太大的耻辱。

sentences.en: So, they're in for the long haul.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们必须坚持到底。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I think there is a recognition that, you know, they kind of need to up their game.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我认为他们也意识到，你知道，他们需要改进自己的手段。

sentences.en: The repression has gone too far.
sentences.zh: 镇压太过分了。

sentences.en: There's a guilt, there's a kind of an acknowledgement that Boudicca was mistreated,
sentences.zh: 有一种负罪感，有一种对布狄卡受到虐待的承认，

sentences.en: and there's an anxiety that Paulinus, in his reprisals, in the wake of the suppression of Boudicca's rebellion,
sentences.zh: 而且人们担心保利努斯在镇压布狄卡叛乱后的报复行动，

sentences.en: I mean, he is kind of creating a desert, and call it a wilderness, and calling it peace.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他简直是在制造一片荒漠，却称之为和平。

sentences.en: And the man who applies this perspective in the wake of Boudicca's revolt is the new procurator, so the guy who's in charge of the finances of the province.
sentences.zh: 而在布狄卡起义后采取这种观点的人是新的财务官，也就是负责该省财政的人。

sentences.en: And this is a man called Gaius Julius Alpinus Classicanus.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫盖乌斯·尤利乌斯·阿尔皮努斯·克拉西卡努斯。
zh_words: 盖乌斯·尤利乌斯·阿尔皮努斯·克拉西卡努斯

sentences.en: You know, so the Alpinus points to the fact that he's from southern Gaul in the region of the Alps.
sentences.zh: 你知道，阿尔皮努斯这个名字表明他来自高卢南部的阿尔卑斯地区。

sentences.en: So maybe that Gallic background suggests why he might feel more sympathetic towards the Britons.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这种高卢背景暗示了他为什么会对不列颠人更具同情心。

sentences.en: He writes back to Rome, he writes to Nero, and he says, look, this is all going too far.
sentences.zh: 他写信回罗马，写给尼禄，说，看，这一切都太过分了。

sentences.en: It's counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 这适得其反。

sentences.en: You need to replace Suetonus Paulinus, even though he's the great general.
sentences.zh: 你需要撤换苏埃托尼乌斯·保利努斯，尽管他是一位伟大的将军。
zh_words: 苏埃托尼乌斯·保利努斯

sentences.en: And so Nero sends a freedman, a man called Polyclitus, on a kind of fact-finding mission.
sentences.zh: 于是尼禄派了一名被释放的奴隶，一个叫波利克利图斯的人，进行某种实地考察。

sentences.en: Tacitus is very withering about the scale of the size of the mission that is sent.
sentences.zh: 塔西佗对这次考察团的规模非常不屑。

sentences.en: But it obviously does a very, very good job, because it reports back and says, yes, you know, we need a new broom here.
sentences.zh: 但它显然做得非常出色，因为它汇报说，是的，你知道，我们需要在这里进行大扫除。

sentences.en: And so some ships are lost, and so they use this as an excuse to withdraw him and bring him back to Rome.
sentences.zh: 于是，由于一些船只失事，他们以此为借口将他撤职并带回了罗马。

sentences.en: And the new governor is the nephew of Aulus Plautius, who was the original invader, the general, the head of the invasion force, the first governor of Britain.
sentences.zh: 新任总督是奥卢斯·普劳提乌斯的侄子，他最初是入侵者、将军、入侵部队的首领，也是不列颠的第一任总督。

sentences.en: And his nephew is a man called Petronius Tepilianus.
sentences.zh: 他的侄子是一个叫佩特罗尼乌斯·图尔皮利亚努斯的人。
zh_words: 佩特罗尼乌斯·图尔皮利亚努斯

sentences.en: And he and Classicarnus work very hard, essentially, at, you know, healing the wounds, at trying to repair the damage.
sentences.zh: 他和克拉西卡努斯非常努力地工作，本质上是为了治愈创伤，试图修复损害。

sentences.en: And they don't engage in fresh conquests.
sentences.zh: 他们没有进行新的征服。

sentences.en: So no further wars under Tepilianus' term of governorship.
sentences.zh: 所以在图尔皮利亚努斯的总督任期内没有发生新的战争。

sentences.en: And Classicarnus himself, already London has become the financial centre.
sentences.zh: 而克拉西卡努斯本人，当时伦敦已经成为了金融中心。

sentences.en: London had been obliterated by Boudicca.
sentences.zh: 伦敦曾被布狄卡夷为平地。

sentences.en: Classicarnus clearly devotes himself to rebuilding it, because he can recognise that it's essentially the natural place from which to administer the finances of Britain.
sentences.zh: 克拉西卡努斯显然致力于重建它，因为他认识到这里本质上是管理不列颠财政的天然场所。

sentences.en: And when he dies in due course in 65, he's given this sumptuous funerary monument in the East End.
sentences.zh: 当他在65年去世时，他在东区获得了一座豪华的墓葬纪念碑。

sentences.en: So beyond the eastern flank of the city, as the road leads out.
sentences.zh: 就在城市东翼之外，道路延伸出去的地方。

sentences.en: And we know that because it was subsequently used as part of the medieval wall and found in excavations.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点是因为它后来被用作中世纪城墙的一部分，并在挖掘中被发现。

sentences.en: And the original is in the British Museum, and there's a replica of it by Tower Hill Tube Station.
sentences.zh: 原件在大英博物馆，塔山地铁站旁有一个复制品。

sentences.en: So you can go and see that if you're passing Tower Hill Tube Station.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你经过塔山地铁站，可以去看看。

sentences.en: Poor Tepilianus comes to a much stickier end.
sentences.zh: 可怜的图尔皮利亚努斯的结局要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: So he goes back to Rome in 63 and is greeted with great honour by Nero.
sentences.zh: 他在63年回到罗马，受到了尼禄的隆重欢迎。

sentences.en: It's generally felt to have done a good job.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为他做得很好。

sentences.en: And so in 68, when rebellion breaks out across the empire against Nero,
sentences.zh: 所以到了68年，当帝国各地爆发反对尼禄的叛乱时，

sentences.en: Nero turns to Tepilianus and puts him in charge of the defence of Italy.
sentences.zh: 尼禄求助于图尔皮利亚努斯，让他负责意大利的防御。

sentences.en: And Nero then commits suicide, and AD 69 sees a whole host of emperors, four in total, succeeding one another.
sentences.zh: 随后尼禄自杀，公元69年见证了许多皇帝，总共四位，相继登基。

sentences.en: And poor Tepilianus gets put to death by the first of these emperors, a man called Galba.
sentences.zh: 而可怜的图尔皮利亚努斯被这些皇帝中的第一位，一个叫加尔巴的人处死了。

sentences.en: But Galba doesn't last very long.
sentences.zh: 但加尔巴没能坚持太久。

sentences.en: His successor, Otho, doesn't last very long.
sentences.zh: 他的继任者奥托也没能坚持太久。

sentences.en: Then you have Vitellius, and then you have Vespasian coming to power.
sentences.zh: 然后是维特里乌斯，接着是维斯帕先掌权。

sentences.en: And Vespasian, people may remember, was in command of the Second Legion in the original invasion back in AD 43.
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得，维斯帕先在公元43年的最初入侵中指挥第二军团。

sentences.en: And he does know Britain, and he kind of pacifies the empire and puts it back on its feet.
sentences.zh: 他确实了解不列颠，他平定了帝国并使其恢复了元气。

sentences.en: But this year, AD 69, the year of the four emperors, has been turbulent for Britain.
sentences.zh: 但这一年，公元69年，四帝之年，对不列颠来说是动荡的。

sentences.en: There are kind of mutinies.
sentences.zh: 发生了各种兵变。

sentences.en: There are different legionary commanders backing different emperors.
sentences.zh: 不同的军团指挥官支持不同的皇帝。

sentences.en: You get one of the legions is completely withdrawn.
sentences.zh: 其中一个军团被完全撤走了。

sentences.en: And so what had been a garrison of four legions now consists of only three.
sentences.zh: 因此，原本四个军团的驻军现在只剩下三个。

sentences.en: And this, in turn, encourages an uprising against Rome in the kingdom of the Brigantes, which, again, we talked about before.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又鼓励了布里甘特人王国对罗马的起义，我们之前也谈到过。

sentences.en: It's essentially northern, what's now northern England, ruled by this extraordinary queen, Carta Mandua, who had been consistently pro-Roman.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是现在的英格兰北部，由这位非凡的女王卡尔塔·曼杜阿统治，她一直亲罗马。

sentences.en: And she was the person who had handed Caraticus over, the great, you know, original freedom fighter in Britain, to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 她就是那个把卡拉塔库斯——不列颠最初伟大的自由战士——交给罗马人的人。

sentences.en: And she has this extraordinary stronghold in North Yorkshire, a place called Stanwyck.
sentences.zh: 她在北约克郡有一个非凡的据点，一个叫斯坦威克的地方。

sentences.en: Very kind of formidable, great ramparts, four miles long in length, lots of high-quality Roman goods.
sentences.zh: 非常险峻，有巨大的城墙，长达四英里，还有许多高质量的罗马商品。

sentences.en: Carta Mandua is clearly absolutely living her best life there, having a fabulous time.
sentences.zh: 卡尔塔·曼杜阿显然在那里过着最好的生活，玩得很开心。

sentences.en: It's all great.
sentences.zh: 一切都很棒。

sentences.en: But she does have problems with her erstwhile husband, who's a man called Venutius.
sentences.zh: 但她确实和她的前夫维努提乌斯有些问题。

sentences.en: And 10 years previously, Venutius and Carta Mandua had had a massive bust-up.
sentences.zh: 10年前，维努提乌斯和卡尔塔·曼杜阿大吵了一架。

sentences.en: Carta Mandua had kicked him out after he'd gone to war with her.
sentences.zh: 在他向她宣战后，卡尔塔·曼杜阿把他赶走了。

sentences.en: The Romans had come to her rescue.
sentences.zh: 罗马人曾来救她。

sentences.en: But Venutius is still kind of lurking there on the margins, keen to make a comeback,
sentences.zh: 但维努提乌斯仍然潜伏在边缘，渴望东山再起，

sentences.en: and is all the more aggravated because Carta Mandua has massively sassed Venutius by having an affair with his armour-bearer, a man called Velocartus.
sentences.zh: 而且因为卡尔塔·曼杜阿与他的武器保管员，一个叫维洛卡图斯的人有染，这让他更加愤怒。

sentences.en: Venutius is really furious, and he takes full advantage of the turmoil in AD69 to have another crack at Carta Mandua to, you know, finish off his ex-wife.
sentences.zh: 维努提乌斯非常愤怒，他充分利用了公元69年的动荡，再次向卡尔塔·曼杜阿发起进攻，想要解决掉他的前妻。

sentences.en: Carta Mandua again appeals for help, and she's rescued in the nick of time by the new governor,
sentences.zh: 卡尔塔·曼杜阿再次求援，并在千钧一发之际被新任总督救出，

sentences.en: who's been sent out by Vitellius III of the emperors in the year of the four emperors.
sentences.zh: 那是四帝之年里，由第三位皇帝维特里乌斯派出的。

sentences.en: And this is a man called Vitellius Balanus, who is actually very, very effective.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫维特里乌斯·巴拉努斯，他实际上非常、非常能干。

sentences.en: And he's so effective that even though Vitellius is the emperor who gets overthrown by Vespasian,
sentences.zh: 他非常能干，以至于尽管维特里乌斯是被维斯帕先推翻的皇帝，

sentences.en: Vespasian is happy to keep Balanus in poSt.
sentences.zh: 维斯帕先却乐于让巴拉努斯留任。

sentences.en: And I guess the reason for that is that he rates Balanus highly, and it doesn't matter that Balanus was appointed by Vitellius,
sentences.zh: 我想原因是他很看重巴拉努斯，而且巴拉努斯是由维特里乌斯任命的并不重要，

sentences.en: because what really matters to Vespasian is that Britain is properly sorted out.
sentences.zh: 因为对维斯帕先来说，真正重要的是不列颠被妥善处理。

sentences.en: So it's under Balanus that the north is pacified,
sentences.zh: 所以是在巴拉努斯的治理下，北方得到了平定，

sentences.en: and he's meant to have done really well, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他应该做得非常好，不是吗？

sentences.en: So I read the poet Statius says he reaches Caledonian fields.
sentences.zh: 我读到诗人斯塔提乌斯说他抵达了喀里多尼亚的田野。

sentences.en: So is Balanus the first Roman to travel to Scotland?
sentences.zh: 那么巴拉努斯是第一个前往苏格兰的罗马人吗？

sentences.en: That's the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 可能不是。

sentences.en: So this is probably poetic exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 所以这很可能是诗意的夸张。

sentences.en: But probably what he is doing is sending diplomatic missions up to Caledonia, so beyond what is now northern England into the lowlands.
sentences.zh: 但他可能是在向喀里多尼亚派遣外交使团，也就是越过现在的英格兰北部进入低地。

sentences.en: And the aim is clearly to try and set up friendly relations with the peoples who live up there.
sentences.zh: 其目的显然是试图与居住在那里的民族建立友好关系。

sentences.en: And he clearly does a good job because when he goes back in 71,
sentences.zh: 他显然干得很出色，因为当他在71年回去时，

sentences.en: Vespasian gives him patrician rank, which is a very high honour indeed.
sentences.zh: 韦斯巴芗授予了他贵族身份，这确实是一项极高的荣誉。

sentences.en: So he's obviously done well for himself.
sentences.zh: 所以他显然在仕途上很成功。

sentences.en: And I think that the fact that Balanus is putting out feelers north beyond even Brigantia into what would now be Scotland
sentences.zh: 我认为巴拉努斯甚至将触角伸向了布里甘提亚以北，直抵如今的苏格兰地区，

sentences.en: reflects the fact that Vespasian wants to see the whole of Britain conquered.
sentences.zh: 这反映出韦斯巴芗想要征服整个不列颠的决心。

sentences.en: And he feels, you know, he had served there.
sentences.zh: 而且他觉得，你知道，他曾在那里服役过。

sentences.en: His son Titus, who in due course will become emperor himself, he'd served there as well.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子提图斯，日后也将成为皇帝，也曾在那里服役。

sentences.en: The Flavian dynasty they're called.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为弗拉维王朝。

sentences.en: The Flavians, I think, see it as the mission they've been given by the gods to conquer Britain.
sentences.zh: 我认为，弗拉维家族将征服不列颠视为神赋予他们的使命。

sentences.en: And there is one further person who is part of the Flavian kind of family dynastic setup who has been engaged in Britain.
sentences.zh: 还有一个人，作为弗拉维家族王朝体系的一部分，也曾参与过不列颠的事务。

sentences.en: And this is our old friend Kerialis, who was the commander of the Ninth Legion
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的老朋友克里亚利斯，他曾是第九军团的指挥官，

sentences.en: that had been mauled by the Icane and the Trinovantes when he was marching to try and relieve Camelodonum.
sentences.zh: 当他行军试图解救卡姆罗多努姆时，曾遭到爱西尼人和特里诺文特人的重创。

sentences.en: And he is the son-in-law of Vespasian.
sentences.zh: 他是韦斯巴芗的女婿。

sentences.en: So he's married Vespasian's daughter.
sentences.zh: 他娶了韦斯巴芗的女儿。

sentences.en: And when Balanus is called back, Vespasian sends Kerialis as the new governor.
sentences.zh: 当巴拉努斯被召回时，韦斯巴芗派克里亚利斯担任新总督。

sentences.en: And you might think this is quite a weird choice considering that he, you know, notoriously been defeated by the Britons.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得这是一个相当奇怪的选择，考虑到他众所周知曾被不列颠人击败过。

sentences.en: But I think Vespasian values him not just because he's obviously very loyal, because he's part of, you know, his family, but also because he's very energetic.
sentences.zh: 但我认为韦斯巴芗看重他，不仅因为他显然非常忠诚，因为他是他家族的一员，还因为他非常有活力。

sentences.en: He's very bold.
sentences.zh: 他非常大胆。

sentences.en: He's not a man to kind of frouse around in his legionary base.
sentences.zh: 他不是那种在军团基地里无所事事的人。

sentences.en: He wants to get out there and crack on.
sentences.zh: 他想走出去，大干一场。

sentences.en: And so Kerialis has proved his worth as a military man by suppressing a rebellion by the Batavians,
sentences.zh: 克里亚利斯通过镇压巴达维人的叛乱证明了自己的军事价值，

sentences.en: who are those Germans who serve the Romans as auxiliaries and can swim across rivers and lakes in their armour.
sentences.zh: 那些德国人作为辅助部队为罗马人效力，甚至能穿着盔甲游过河流和湖泊。

sentences.en: And they had perhaps rebelled.
sentences.zh: 他们或许曾经叛乱过。

sentences.en: It's unclear exactly the degree to which they'd rebelled or they'd been embroiled in the civil war.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚他们叛乱的程度，或者他们是否卷入了内战。

sentences.en: But anyway, Kerialis had pacified Batavia and he's now come to Britain.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，克里亚利斯平定了巴达维亚，现在他来到了不列颠。

sentences.en: And it's an indication of how determined Vespasian is to see Britain conquered,
sentences.zh: 韦斯巴芗决心征服不列颠，这从一个迹象可以看出：

sentences.en: that when Kerialis comes to Britain, he does so with a legion so that the strength of the island's garrison is restored from three to four.
sentences.zh: 当克里亚利斯来到不列颠时，他带来了一个军团，使得岛上的驻军力量从三个军团增加到了四个。

sentences.en: So it's all go.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都在推进中。

sentences.en: So his plan is to go up he goes by the 71.
sentences.zh: 他的计划是向北推进，他在71年出发。

sentences.en: So that year that he arrives, he goes up past the Midlands.
sentences.zh: 他抵达的那一年，他越过了中部地区。

sentences.en: He goes up north of the Humber.
sentences.zh: 他向亨伯河以北进发。

sentences.en: He goes to the River Ouse and he's heading towards the place that we would now call York.
sentences.zh: 他到达了乌兹河，正朝着我们现在称为约克的地方前进。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Previously, the most northerly base was Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 此前，最北端的基地是林肯。

sentences.en: He now wants to push further forwards.
sentences.zh: 他现在想进一步向前推进。

sentences.en: And on the site of York or Eberarchum, as the Romans call it, the place of yew trees,
sentences.zh: 在约克或罗马人称之为埃伯拉库姆（意为紫杉之地）的地方，

sentences.en: apparently it means in Britonic, is strategically a very good one because it's on the obvious route for marching northwards, the Great Northern Road, as it will come to be called.
sentences.zh: 在布立吞语中显然是这个意思，从战略上讲是一个非常好的位置，因为它位于向北行军的必经之路上，也就是后来被称为大北路的地方。

sentences.en: But it can also be supplied by sea up the Humber.
sentences.zh: 而且它也可以通过亨伯河从海上获得补给。

sentences.en: And so this becomes the new base for the Ninth Legion.
sentences.zh: 于是这里成为了第九军团的新基地。

sentences.en: So it moves up from Lincoln to York.
sentences.zh: 所以它从林肯迁到了约克。

sentences.en: And it's obviously a launch pad for further expansion northwards.
sentences.zh: 这显然是进一步向北扩张的发射台。

sentences.en: So over the term of Kerialis's governorship, there are clearly repeated battles on both sides of the Pennines.
sentences.zh: 因此，在克里亚利斯担任总督期间，奔宁山脉两侧显然发生了多次战斗。

sentences.en: You know, the great spine of uplands that runs up northern Britain, northern England.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那条贯穿不列颠北部和英格兰北部的高地脊梁。

sentences.en: And by 72, you have a fort being established in what will become Carlisle.
sentences.zh: 到了72年，在后来成为卡莱尔的地方建立了一座堡垒。

sentences.en: So almost on the doorstep of what today is Scotland.
sentences.zh: 几乎就在今天苏格兰的门口。

sentences.en: And in 74, Kerialis is replaced by a very, very impressive man called Frontinus, who wrote a number of works that have survived.
sentences.zh: 74年，克里亚利斯被一位非常令人印象深刻的人弗朗提努斯取代，他写过许多流传至今的著作。

sentences.en: He was clearly a very proficient engineer.
sentences.zh: 他显然是一位非常精通的工程师。

sentences.en: So he wrote an excellent book on aqueducts, which is our main source for how aqueducts functioned.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本关于渡槽的优秀著作，这是我们了解渡槽运作方式的主要来源。

sentences.en: A huge inspiration to Robert Harris, Dominic, who you talked to on a bonus, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你之前在特别节目中采访过他，这对罗伯特·哈里斯来说是一个巨大的灵感来源，不是吗？

sentences.en: He wrote a book about Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本关于庞贝的书。

sentences.en: And Frotinus' book on aqueducts was a massive source for Robert Harris when he was writing that.
sentences.zh: 弗朗提努斯关于渡槽的书是罗伯特·哈里斯写作时的重要参考资料。

sentences.en: Very concerned with how you repair leaks, which is one of the themes that runs throughout that novel.
sentences.zh: 他非常关注如何修复泄漏，这也是贯穿那部小说的主题之一。

sentences.en: He's also very much a military man.
sentences.zh: 他也是一位地道的军人。

sentences.en: So he wrote a book on military stratagems through the ages.
sentences.zh: 所以他写了一本关于历代军事策略的书。

sentences.en: And in doing that, he could boast a very formidable track record because he is setting out to absolutely pacify two upland areas
sentences.zh: 在做这些事的同时，他可以夸耀自己拥有非常辉煌的战绩，因为他着手彻底平定两个高地地区，

sentences.en: that are on the doorsteps of the kind of the lowlands, which is Brigantia and Wales.
sentences.zh: 这两个地区就在低地的门口，分别是布里甘提亚和威尔士。

sentences.en: So Brigantia pretty much has been pacified by 77, except perhaps in the Lake District, you know, Helvellyn and all that, very difficult to sort out.
sentences.zh: 到77年，布里甘提亚基本上已经被平定，除了湖区，你知道，赫尔维林山那一带，非常难搞。

sentences.en: So people who've been to the Lake District may have visited the Roman fort at Hard Knot.
sentences.zh: 去过湖区的人可能参观过哈德诺特的罗马堡垒。

sentences.en: That's built, you know, several decades later.
sentences.zh: 那是几十年后才建的。

sentences.en: It's a sign that that is the one region of Northern England that remains difficult for the Romans to pin down.
sentences.zh: 这表明那是英格兰北部唯一一个罗马人难以掌控的地区。

sentences.en: And of course, Wales has been a constant source of stress for a succession of governors and Frotinus.
sentences.zh: 当然，威尔士一直是历任总督和弗朗提努斯头疼的根源。

sentences.en: He's doing his bit.
sentences.zh: 他尽了自己的职责。

sentences.en: So he found two massive new legionary fortresses, one at Celyon and one at Chester.
sentences.zh: 他建立了两个巨大的新军团要塞，一个在卡利恩，一个在切斯特。

sentences.en: The Roman remains in those two sites are still very impressive to this day.
sentences.zh: 这两个遗址的罗马遗迹至今仍令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: More forts across Wales.
sentences.zh: 威尔士各地还有更多的堡垒。

sentences.en: And the reason why I think Frotinus is particularly interested in seeing Wales pacified is because as an engineer, he's interested in all the mineral wealth
sentences.zh: 我认为弗朗提努斯之所以特别热衷于平定威尔士，是因为作为一名工程师，他对威尔士所能提供的所有矿产财富很感兴趣，

sentences.en: that Wales has to offer, all the gold, the silver, the lead and so on.
sentences.zh: 所有的黄金、白银、铅等等。

sentences.en: And so he's absolutely determined to secure them.
sentences.zh: 所以他绝对决心要确保这些资源的安全。

sentences.en: So on this, people like Frotinus, my sense had always been that Britain was a complete backwater in the Roman Empire and that basically a posting there was a, it was a demotion,
sentences.zh: 关于弗朗提努斯这类人，我一直觉得不列颠在罗马帝国中是一个完全的偏远地区，基本上被派到那里是一种降职，

sentences.en: like being sent to run one of Goldhanger's other podcasts, Tom.
sentences.zh: 就像被派去管理高尔汉格的其他播客一样，汤姆。

sentences.en: But no, Britain is the rest is history of the Roman stable.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此，不列颠是罗马帝国历史的一部分。

sentences.en: Is it?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Because actually some of the people who are being sent to run Britain are absolutely tip-top people.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，一些被派去管理不列颠的人都是顶尖人才。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, of course, there are kind of recalcitrant and turbulent elements in the rest of history who need a whip hand to rein them in.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，历史的其他部分中确实存在一些顽固和动荡的分子，需要铁腕来约束他们。

sentences.en: So maybe to that extent.
sentences.zh: 所以也许在某种程度上是这样。

sentences.en: I think there's a sense that Britain is the most challenging province to administer.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们普遍认为不列颠是最难管理的省份。

sentences.en: And so it's not Syria or Egypt, which really are the kind of the plum postings because you can get rich there, basically, and it's not going to be too stressful.
sentences.zh: 所以它不是叙利亚或埃及，那些才是真正的肥差，因为你在那里基本上可以发财，而且不会太有压力。

sentences.en: But Britain is where you send your most competent people, the guys you can trust to do a good job.
sentences.zh: 但不列颠是你派遣最能干的人的地方，那些你可以信任去完成出色工作的人。

sentences.en: And that reflects the fact that in Britain, a governor needs to be a very proficient general.
sentences.zh: 这反映了一个事实，即在不列颠，总督必须是一位非常精通的将军。

sentences.en: There's a lot of fighting to do, but you also need to be very good as a civil administrator.
sentences.zh: 有很多仗要打，但你也必须非常擅长民事管理。

sentences.en: So that's where Suetonius Paulinus fell down.
sentences.zh: 这就是苏托尼乌斯·保利努斯失败的地方。

sentences.en: He was a brilliant general, but he was absolutely hopeless at kind of pacifying territories that had been conquered
sentences.zh: 他是一位出色的将军，但在平定被征服领土方面却完全无能，

sentences.en: and kind of introducing them to civilization, as the Romans would define it.
sentences.zh: 无法像罗马人所定义的那样将他们引入文明。

sentences.en: By the 70s, you have the war zone in the north.
sentences.zh: 到了70年代，北部成为了战区。

sentences.en: This is targeted for conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 这是征服的目标。

sentences.en: But by this period, the lowlands in the south are starting to recover from the depredations of the conquest and Boudicca's rebellion.
sentences.zh: 但到了这个时期，南部的低地开始从征服和布狄卡起义的破坏中恢复过来。

sentences.en: This matters because you can't essentially fund the campaigns that have to be launched without extracting a bit of wealth from the lowland provinces.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为如果不从低地省份榨取一点财富，你就无法资助必须发起的战役。

sentences.en: You know, you need that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你需要那个。

sentences.en: So that's why I think in 77, when Frontinus is recalled by Vespasian, he sends, as the new governor, a man who really couldn't be better qualified for the job.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么我认为在77年，当弗朗提努斯被韦斯巴芗召回时，他派去了一位再合适不过的新总督。

sentences.en: So this is a man called Gnaeus Julius Agricola.
sentences.zh: 这就是格奈乌斯·尤利乌斯·阿古利可拉。
zh_words: 格奈乌斯·尤利乌斯·阿古利可拉

sentences.en: We've mentioned him at various points throughout the series so far, but just to give a bit more background on him, he comes from a long line of Roman citizens in southern Gaul.

sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，展望未来，当罗马在不列颠的统治崩溃时，这些城镇会很快变得破败不堪。

sentences.en: So in other words, their foundations are very shallow from the very beginning, because you said looking ahead.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它们的根基从一开始就很浅，因为你提到了展望未来。

sentences.en: I mean, you're looking three centuries ahead or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是在展望三个世纪之后或更久。

sentences.en: In all that time, they don't really put down enough, deep enough roots to survive once the colonial power has gone.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，它们并没有真正扎下足够深的根，以至于在殖民力量撤走后还能生存。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's why, you know, again, Tacitus is bigging up Agricola, but I'm sure it's not just Agricola.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，塔西佗在吹捧阿古利可拉，但我肯定不只是阿古利可拉一人在做这些事。

sentences.en: All the governors are doing it.
sentences.zh: 所有的总督都在做。

sentences.en: But Tacitus says of Agricola, he gave private encouragement and official assistance to the building of temples, public squares and good houses, because it wouldn't happen without
sentences.zh: 但塔西佗谈到阿古利可拉时说，他给予私人鼓励和官方援助，以建造神庙、公共广场和良好的住宅，因为没有罗马的鼓励，这一切都不会发生。

sentences.en: Roman encouragement.
sentences.zh: 我们还没谈到到底有多少罗马人在不列颠。

sentences.en: We've not talked at all about how many Romans actually are in Britain.
sentences.zh: 人们大概不会自愿大量移居到不列颠。

sentences.en: People don't move to Britain voluntarily, presumably, in great numbers.
sentences.zh: 我想如果是商人或供应商，他们会去。

sentences.en: I think they do if they're merchants, if they're suppliers.
sentences.zh: 当然还有军队。

sentences.en: Of course, the military.
sentences.zh: 我们看到许多退伍军人在卡姆罗多努姆定居。

sentences.en: We saw lots of veterans settling at Camlidonum.
sentences.zh: 那次结果并不好。

sentences.en: That didn't work out well.
sentences.zh: 但退伍军人依然在这样做。

sentences.en: But veterans continue to do that.
sentences.zh: 但人们通常不会坐在西班牙、法国南部或其他地方说：“我想搬到不列颠去。”

sentences.en: But people aren't generally sitting there in Spain or southern France or somewhere and saying, I'd like to move to Britain.
sentences.zh: 不，他们不会。

sentences.en: No, they're not.
sentences.zh: 因为那里有什么吸引你的？

sentences.en: Because what's there for you?
sentences.zh: 不列颠一直被罗马人，尤其是罗马统治阶级所鄙视，直到最后。

sentences.en: Britain remains despised by the Romans, certainly the Roman ruling classes, right up to the end.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在四世纪末，高卢的诗人们依然觉得，像西塞罗那样在不列颠有个诗人简直是滑稽可笑。

sentences.en: So even in the late fourth century, you have poets in Gaul who just find it hilarious, the idea that, you know, you might have a poet in Britain, like Cicero had been.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，什么都没有真正改变。

sentences.en: I mean, nothing has really changed.
sentences.zh: 我认为不列颠作为边疆国家的观念一直存在。

sentences.en: And I think the sense of Britain as a frontier state, it endures.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫斯图尔特·莱科克的人写了一本书叫《不列颠尼亚：失败的国家》，还有另一本关于罗马不列颠的书，他在书中主要论证了部落

sentences.en: So there's a guy called Stuart Laycock who wrote a book called Britannia, Failed State, and then another book on Roman Britain, in which he essentially argues that the tribal
sentences.zh: 群体的存在方式比人们想象的要稳固得多，而罗马统治的根基极其浅薄。

sentences.en: groupings persist in a much stronger way than people have thought, and that the foundations of Roman rule are incredibly shallow.
sentences.zh: 但同样，不列颠将永远有重兵把守。

sentences.en: But equally, Britain will always be heavily garrisoned.
sentences.zh: 这意味着只要那里有成功的军队，就有机会在那里植入一种古典地中海文明的模拟物。

sentences.en: And so that means that as long as there are successful armies there, there are opportunities for a kind of simulacrum of classical Mediterranean civilisation to be planted there.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为，重申一遍，如果你想建立一个正规的税收体系，就需要这些城市中心。

sentences.en: And that matters because, you know, just to reiterate, you need these urban centres if you are going to have a proper taxation system.
sentences.zh: 而税收体系对于行省的成功运作至关重要。

sentences.en: And taxation system is crucial to the successful functioning of the province.
sentences.zh: 在罗马人的观念中，没有人口普查就无法建立税收体系。

sentences.en: And you can't have a taxation system in the Roman opinion without a census.
sentences.zh: 我们从《新约》中也知道这一点。

sentences.en: So we know that from, you know, from the New Testament.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么圣家族前往伯利恒的故事听起来有那么一点可信度。

sentences.en: It's why the story of the holy family going to Bethlehem is kind of faintly credible.
sentences.zh: 无论罗马人走到哪里，他们都会进行人口普查。

sentences.en: And wherever the Romans go, they hold a census.
sentences.zh: 塔西佗告诉我们，阿古利可拉也做了这件事。

sentences.en: Agricola, we're told by Tacitus, does this.
sentences.zh: 记录被汇编并存储在伦敦，那里已经成为了金融中心。

sentences.en: Records are compiled, stored in London, which has already become the financial capital.
sentences.zh: 而且，以现代前系统的标准来看，这非常了不起。

sentences.en: And, you know, by the standards of a pre-modern system, this is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种非常、非常复杂的从被征服人民身上榨取钱财的框架，并为后来的帝国体系提供了模板。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a very, very sophisticated framework for extorting money out of conquered peoples and provides a kind of template for subsequent imperial systeMs.
sentences.zh: 这也为阿古利可拉的任期建立了一个模板。

sentences.en: And it establishes a template as well for Agricola's terms of office.
sentences.zh: 冬天，他忙于修建浴场、进行人口普查和处理税收。

sentences.en: So in the winter, he operates on building baths or, you know, holding censuses and sorting out tacks.
sentences.zh: 夏天，他就去打仗。

sentences.en: And the summer, he goes off to war.
sentences.zh: 这就是他最著名的伟大工程。

sentences.en: So this is the great project for which he's best known.
sentences.zh: 韦斯巴芗交给他的使命，即征服喀里多尼亚。

sentences.en: The mission that Vespasian has given him, which is the conquest of Caledonia.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，弗拉维王朝将此视为神赋予他们的使命。

sentences.en: As you said, the Flavian dynasty see this as their mission from the gods.
sentences.zh: 当然，韦斯巴芗在79年去世了。

sentences.en: Of course, Vespasian dies in 79.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子提图斯继位。

sentences.en: He's succeeded by his son Titus.
sentences.zh: 提图斯有点像任何一位新皇帝，有点像克劳狄。

sentences.en: And Titus is a little bit like, I guess, any new emperor, a bit like Claudius.
sentences.zh: 因为在这个故事的开头，他需要征服带来的推动力来赋予他合法性。

sentences.en: Because right at the beginning of this story, he needs the boost of conquest to give him legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 所以这大概就是阿古利可拉事业背后的动机。

sentences.en: And so that presumably lies behind Agricola's enterprise.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 到了80年，也就是提图斯统治的第二年，他在罗马落成了斗兽场。

sentences.en: And by 80, so that's the second year of Titus's rule, when he inaugurates the Colosseum back in Rome.
sentences.zh: 落成典礼上展出的野兽之一就是来自喀里多尼亚的熊。

sentences.en: One of the beasts that is featured in the inaugural games is a bear from Caledonia.
sentences.zh: 有一个罪犯被钉在十字架上，熊被诱导去吞食他的内脏。

sentences.en: There's a criminal who's kind of crucified and the bear is encouraged to devour his intestines.
sentences.zh: 这被认为是非常令人兴奋的。

sentences.en: And this is seen as all very exciting.
sentences.zh: 事实上，将一只来自喀里多尼亚的熊囚禁在竞技场内，象征性地向罗马人民展示了，

sentences.en: And the fact that you have a bear from Caledonia imprisoned within the arena symbolically is
sentences.zh: 不仅是野兽，连那片土地和生活在土地上的人民现在都已经臣服了。

sentences.en: an illustration to the Roman people that not just the beasts, but the land and the peoples that live on the land have now been subordinated.
sentences.zh: 这被视为一项了不起的壮举，因为对罗马地理学家来说，喀里多尼亚是野蛮的缩影。

sentences.en: And this is seen as an amazing feat because to Roman geographers, Caledonia is the epitome of barbarism.
sentences.zh: 他们将其描述为一片连绵不断的森林，当然事实并非如此。

sentences.en: They describe it as being one continual forest, which, of course, it isn't.
sentences.zh: 但通过将其描绘成森林，他们本质上是在说，那里简直是地狱。

sentences.en: But by casting it as a forest, they're essentially saying, you know, it is absolutely the pits.
sentences.zh: 他们完全理所当然地认为那里的居民极其野蛮。

sentences.en: They completely take for granted that its inhabitants are beyond savage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些蛮族甚至比南部的不列颠人骨架还要大。

sentences.en: You know, these are barbarians who are even larger boned than the Britons in the south.
sentences.zh: 他们长着橘红色的头发。

sentences.en: They're orange haired.
sentences.zh: 庞波尼乌斯·梅拉，一位克劳狄时期的地理学家，他描述

sentences.en: Pomponius Mailer, who's a geographer writing back in the time of Claudius, he describes the
sentences.zh: 喀里多尼亚的居民粗鲁无礼，比世界上任何地方的人都更不懂得什么是文明，几乎完全不尊重神灵。

sentences.en: inhabitants of Caledonia as being uncouth, more ignorant of what makes for civilization than people anywhere in the world, almost wholly lacking in respect for the gods.
sentences.zh: 而“喀里多尼亚”的字面意思似乎是“强悍的人，贫瘠的土地”。

sentences.en: And the literal meaning of Caledonia seems to be hard men, hard land.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像那种“苏格兰制造，坚固耐用”的形象。

sentences.en: Yeah, made in Scotland from girders, that kind of image.
sentences.zh: 而且橘红色的头发，他们很早就注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: And the orange hair, they pick up on the orange hair so early on.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 所以到了81年，也就是他任期的第四年，阿古利可拉已经稳固了一条横跨克莱德河和福斯河的边境线。

sentences.en: So by 81, which is four years into his term of office, Agricola has secured a frontier that is spanning the Clyde and the Forth.
sentences.zh: 那基本上就在爱丁堡和格拉斯哥之间。

sentences.en: So that's basically between Edinburgh and Glasgow.
sentences.zh: 现在那里就是安东尼长城未来所在的地方。

sentences.en: Now it's where the Antonine Wall will run in due course.
sentences.zh: 从这里，他有能力去窥探北方的喀里多尼亚、高地，还有爱尔兰，你知道，那离得不远，从苏格兰南端就能看到。

sentences.en: And from here, he's in a position to scope out, you know, Caledonia to the north, the highlands, but also Ireland, you know, which isn't far, kind of within, you know, you can
sentences.zh: 在阿古利可拉时代，爱尔兰对不列颠的关系，就像尤利乌斯·凯撒时代不列颠对高卢的关系一样。

sentences.en: see it from the southern tip of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像凯撒时代一样，前往不列颠的商人可以向高卢的帝国当局报告。

sentences.en: And Ireland in Agricola's time is to Britain, what Britain was to Gaul back in Julius Caesar's time.
sentences.zh: 所以你有罗马商人前往爱尔兰并向阿古利可拉报告。

sentences.en: So, you know, as in Caesar's time, merchants going to Britain can report back to the imperial authorities in Gaul.
sentences.zh: 阿古利可拉已经与各爱尔兰领袖建立了友好条约。

sentences.en: So you have merchants, Roman merchants going to Ireland and reporting back to Agricola.
sentences.zh: 有一位被驱逐的爱尔兰国王向阿古利可拉寻求庇护，请求他干预。

sentences.en: And Agricola has established treaties of friendship with various Irish leaders.
sentences.zh: 这在尤利乌斯·凯撒和克劳狄时代都非常常见。

sentences.en: You have an Irish king who's been thrown out, who takes refuge with Agricola, asks him to intervene.
sentences.zh: 这些都是罗马人发动入侵所需要的机会。

sentences.en: So this is very, very familiar from both the time of Julius Caesar and Claudius.
sentences.zh: 事实上，据塔西佗记载，阿古利可拉非常心动。

sentences.en: These are all the opportunities that the Romans need to launch an invasion.
sentences.zh: 所以塔西佗写道，我经常听阿古利可拉说，爱尔兰可以用一个军团加上相当数量的辅助部队来征服并占领，而且这会更容易。

sentences.en: And in fact, according to Tacitus, Agricola was very tempted.
sentences.zh: 而且这会更容易。

sentences.en: So Tacitus writes, I've often heard Agricola say that Ireland could be reduced and held by a single legion with a fair-sized force of auxiliaries, and that it would be easier
sentences.zh: 而且这会更容易。

sentences.en: to hold Britain if it were completely surrounded by Roman armies, so that liberty was banished from its sight.
sentences.zh: 若不列颠被罗马军队完全包围，自由便会从其视野中被放逐，从而掌控不列颠。

sentences.en: Fortunately for the Irish, Agricola decides, you know, he doesn't have time because his focus is Caledonia.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，阿古里科拉认为，你知道，他没有时间，因为他的重心在喀里多尼亚。

sentences.en: That's what Titus, back in Rome, wants him to do.
sentences.zh: 这正是远在罗马的提图斯希望他做的事。

sentences.en: And so Ireland is left alone.
sentences.zh: 于是爱尔兰被留在了原地。

sentences.en: And in 81, when Titus dies and is succeeded by his brother Domitian, and Domitian, unlike
sentences.zh: 公元81年，提图斯去世，其弟图密善继位。与提图斯不同，

sentences.en: Titus, has not served in Britain, in fact, hasn't served in a military context anywhere, he has even more reason to want great military glory that he can trumpet.
sentences.zh: 图密善从未在不列颠服役，事实上，他从未在任何军事环境下服役过，因此他更有理由渴望能大肆宣扬的伟大军事功绩。

sentences.en: And so this means that essentially Agricola has been told, you know, get on with it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着阿古里科拉基本上接到了命令，你知道，继续推进吧。

sentences.en: I want all of Britain conquered.
sentences.zh: 我要征服整个不列颠。

sentences.en: And so this is what Agricola sets out to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿古里科拉着手要做的事情。

sentences.en: And he pursues a two-pronged strategy by land and by sea.
sentences.zh: 他采取了海陆并进的双管齐下的策略。

sentences.en: So by land, advancing along the kind of the lowland strip on the eastern flank of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 陆地上，沿着苏格兰东侧的低地带推进。

sentences.en: So leaving the highlands, you know, the mountainous regions, well alone, he doesn't even attempt to go into them.
sentences.zh: 所以高地，你知道，那些山区，就完全不去管它，他甚至没尝试进入那些地区。

sentences.en: And he reaches almost all the way up to the Murrow Forth, so up to Culloden, of course.
sentences.zh: 他几乎一直推进到了默里湾，当然，也就是到了卡洛登。

sentences.en: What's he find?
sentences.zh: 他发现了什么？

sentences.en: As in, obviously, there's so much we can't know, because there aren't really many written sources other than Tacitus.
sentences.zh: 显然，有很多事情我们无法得知，因为除了塔西佗之外，并没有太多书面资料。

sentences.en: But is that sense that what he finds in what's now Scotland is pretty similar to what he finds
sentences.zh: 但有一种感觉是，他在现在的苏格兰发现的东西，与他在

sentences.en: in Wales or Northern England, i.e. the village settlements, people painted blue, all that kind of stuff?
sentences.zh: 威尔士或英格兰北部发现的非常相似，比如村落、涂成蓝色的人，诸如此类？

sentences.en: Or is it very different?
sentences.zh: 还是说非常不同？

sentences.en: Let me read you what Ronald Hutton in his book, Pagan Britain, has to say on this.
sentences.zh: 让我读读罗纳德·赫顿在他的书《异教不列颠》中对此的看法。

sentences.en: So this is a description of Britain in the late Iron Age, just before the Roman invasion.
sentences.zh: 这是对铁器时代晚期，即罗马入侵前夕不列颠的描述。

sentences.en: And he says, there's the southeast itself, you know, very Romanized, imported Roman or
sentences.zh: 他说，东南部本身，你知道，非常罗马化，进口了罗马或

sentences.en: Roman-style goods.
sentences.zh: 罗马风格的商品。

sentences.en: Then north and west of this area, so the Midlands, Yorkshire, so on, a zone that had smaller settlements and farmsteads, numerous enclosures and a greater emphasis.
sentences.zh: 然后是该区域的北部和西部，即中部地区、约克郡等地，这一带的定居点和农舍较小，围栏众多，且更强调。

sentences.en: So some pastoral farming.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些畜牧业。

sentences.en: The rest of the island, so that would include Wales, and it would certainly include Caledonia,
sentences.zh: 岛屿的其余部分，包括威尔士，当然也包括喀里多尼亚，

sentences.en: exhibited much more continuity with the earlier Iron Age, lacking coins, lacking continental manufacturers, and indeed large central places of assembly.
sentences.zh: 表现出与早期铁器时代更多的延续性，缺乏硬币、缺乏大陆制造品，也缺乏大型的中央集会场所。

sentences.en: So political units, like when Agricola gets into Caledonia, are there tribal strongholds?
sentences.zh: 那么政治单位呢，比如当阿古里科拉进入喀里多尼亚时，那里有部落据点吗？

sentences.en: Are there warlords?
sentences.zh: 有军阀吗？

sentences.en: No, it's kind of homesteads, fortified enclosures on a much, much kind of smaller scale.
sentences.zh: 没有，那儿更像是宅地，规模要小得多、小得多的防御性围栏。

sentences.en: So therefore, on one level, kind of easier to conquer, I suppose, but on another, kind of impossible, because you can't pin them down.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，我想这更容易征服，但从另一方面看，这几乎是不可能的，因为你无法锁定他们。

sentences.en: There's no central authority.
sentences.zh: 那里没有中央权威。

sentences.zh: 没有首都，没有国王，没有什么可以让你占领从而结束战争的东西。

sentences.en: Yes, and you can be kind of lulled by this, I suppose, into thinking that, you know, the
sentences.zh: 是的，你可能会因此产生一种错觉，我想，认为

sentences.zh: 喀里多尼亚人就像蠓虫一样。

sentences.zh: 他们很烦人，但最终对你造成不了多大伤害。

sentences.en: Except, of course, there is always the risk that if you go crashing up there with your legions,
sentences.zh: 当然，除非总是存在一种风险，如果你带着军团冲进那里，

sentences.zh: 这会鼓励那些原本孤立分散的人们聚集起来，试图组成一支游击队，然后攻击入侵者。

sentences.en: And this is actually what happens in 82.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上就发生在公元82年。

sentences.zh: 这是阿古里科拉担任总督的第六年，喀里多尼亚人

sentences.zh: 对倒霉的第九军团发动了夜袭，这支军团总是经常被打得落花流水。

sentences.en: And the 9th Legion is taken by surprise.
sentences.zh: 第九军团被打了个措手不及。

sentences.en: Their camp might almost have been overrun, except that Agricola is able to come and reinforce them.
sentences.zh: 他们的营地差点就被攻破了，幸好阿古里科拉及时赶到并增援了他们。

sentences.en: And Agricola turns it to his own ends by saying, well, look, you know, you've been given a bloody nose.
sentences.zh: 阿古里科拉利用这一点达到了自己的目的，他说，看，你知道，你们吃了败仗。

sentences.en: We've got to get on and get revenge for that.
sentences.zh: 我们必须继续前进，为那次失败复仇。

sentences.en: And the 9th and all the other legions go cheer and say, yeah, let's get there.
sentences.zh: 第九军团和其他所有军团都欢呼起来，说，好，让我们去吧。

sentences.en: Let's get to the ends of the world.
sentences.zh: 让我们到达世界的尽头。

sentences.en: And according to Tacitus, this is how Agricola gets his men to share in the dream of conquering the whole of Britain.
sentences.zh: 据塔西佗记载，阿古里科拉就是这样让他的士兵们分享征服整个不列颠的梦想的。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's a challenge.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一个挑战。

sentences.en: There's no question about it.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But Agricola has his instructions.
sentences.zh: 但阿古里科拉有他的指令。

sentences.en: And so the building of infrastructure, roads, forts, it's worked in Wales.
sentences.zh: 所以基础设施、道路、堡垒的建设，在威尔士行之有效。

sentences.en: There's no obvious reason why it wouldn't work in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 没有明显的理由说明它在苏格兰行不通。

sentences.en: And there's also an additional factor, which is that Agricola has got a fleet.
sentences.zh: 还有一个额外的因素，那就是阿古里科拉拥有一支舰队。

sentences.en: And this is central to his whole plan because it means that his army can be supplied by sea
sentences.zh: 这对他的整个计划至关重要，因为这意味着他的军队可以通过海路获得补给，

sentences.en: and also that the fleet can be used to kind of ferry small groups of soldiers up and down to wherever they're needed.
sentences.zh: 而且舰队还可以用来将小股士兵运送到任何需要他们的地方。

sentences.en: So if there's a stronghold, you know, on an isolated promontory or something like that, the soldiers can be taken there.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有一个据点，你知道，在孤立的岬角或其他什么地方，士兵们就可以被带到那里。

sentences.en: Of course, for the Romans who were essentially used to much calmer seas, the North Sea off the Scottish coast can be very, very frightening.
sentences.zh: 当然，对于习惯了平静海面的罗马人来说，苏格兰海岸外的北海可能非常、非常可怕。

sentences.en: And Tacitus describes how soldiers and the sailors, when they meet up, they kind of compete
sentences.zh: 塔西佗描述了士兵和水手们见面时，他们会进行攀比，

sentences.en: by saying, you know, which is more dangerous, the Caledonians or the breakers and the rocks of the sea.
sentences.zh: 说，你知道，到底是喀里多尼亚人更危险，还是海上的碎浪和礁石更危险。

sentences.en: And Tacitus also reports that the Britons themselves, so the people in Caledonia, are much more intimidated by the fleet than they are by the army.
sentences.zh: 塔西佗还报道说，不列颠人自己，也就是喀里多尼亚的人民，对舰队的恐惧远甚于对军队的恐惧。

sentences.en: So he writes, the Britons, for their part, we learned from prisoners, were dismayed by the appearance of the fleet.
sentences.zh: 所以他写道，我们从俘虏那里得知，不列颠人对舰队的出现感到惊恐。

sentences.en: Now that the places of their sea were opened up, they felt that their last refuge in defeat was closed against them.
sentences.zh: 现在他们海上避难的地方被打开了，他们感到在战败时最后的避难所也被封死了。

sentences.en: So by 88, Agricola is ready for what he hopes will be the final push by both land and sea.
sentences.zh: 到了公元88年，阿古里科拉已经准备好进行他所希望的陆海最终攻势了。

sentences.en: So shall I read you what I wrote?
sentences.zh: 要我读读我写的东西吗？

sentences.en: I think everybody would really love that.
sentences.zh: 我想大家一定会很喜欢的。

sentences.en: I think they would.
sentences.zh: 我想他们会喜欢的。

sentences.en: So repeatedly confronted by Roman steel, the Caledonians had melted away into bogs and woods as insubstantial.
sentences.zh: 在罗马钢铁的反复冲击下，喀里多尼亚人像虚无缥缈的东西一样消融在沼泽和森林中。

sentences.en: So it seemed to the frustrated invaders as the cloud that veiled the highland peaks.
sentences.zh: 对于沮丧的入侵者来说，这看起来就像遮蔽高地山峰的云雾。

sentences.en: But now, at last, they were brought to battle.
sentences.zh: 但现在，他们终于被迫投入了战斗。

sentences.en: And this Dominic is Mount Graupius.
sentences.zh: 这就是多米尼克所说的格劳皮乌斯山。

sentences.en: Don't know where it is exactly, but probably in the vicinity of Aberdeen, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 不知道具体在哪里，但可能在阿伯丁附近，或许吧。

sentences.en: And this is where Calgarcus supposedly gives his great talk.
sentences.zh: 这就是卡尔加库斯据称发表他那伟大演讲的地方。

sentences.en: Did he even exist?
sentences.zh: 他真的存在吗？

sentences.en: Don't know.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: Don't know.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a theory that the name is derived from the armour, the swordman, the armour keeper, Venutius, the Brigantian chief.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一种理论认为这个名字源于盔甲，剑客，盔甲守护者，维努提乌斯，布里甘特人的首领。

sentences.en: So that's, I don't know, who knows?
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: But what we do know is that at last, Agricola has managed to encourage the Caledonians to form a kind of coherent army with chariots and everything.
sentences.zh: 但我们所知道的是，阿古里科拉终于成功地鼓励喀里多尼亚人组成了一支拥有战车等装备的连贯军队。

sentences.en: And he's done this essentially by kind of raiding the length of the coastline so that the Caledonians feel they've got no choice but to try and see the invader off in pitch battle.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是通过沿着海岸线突袭来做到这一点的，这样喀里多尼亚人就觉得别无选择，只能尝试在正面战场上击退入侵者。

sentences.en: And they assemble on the foothills of Mount Graupius.
sentences.zh: 他们聚集在格劳皮乌斯山的山脚下。

sentences.en: There's lots of yelling, chanting, cheering, kind of shenanigans with chariots zipping up and down.
sentences.zh: 到处都是叫喊声、吟唱声、欢呼声，还有战车来回穿梭的闹剧。

sentences.en: And then the next day, the battle is joined.
sentences.zh: 第二天，战斗打响了。

sentences.en: And it's actually the Batavians, you know, these German auxiliaries who've been a feature of the conquest right from the very beginning, who take the lead against the enemy.
sentences.zh: 实际上是巴达维亚人，你知道，这些从一开始就是征服主力之一的德国辅助部队，带头对抗敌人。

sentences.en: And then it's the cavalry that finished them off after the legions have essentially kind of cut them to pieces.
sentences.zh: 然后在军团基本上将他们切成碎片后，是骑兵完成了最后的清剿。

sentences.en: And the next day at dawn, Agricola sends horsemen out to reconnoiter the vicinity to see if there's any fighting that needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 第二天黎明，阿古里科拉派出骑兵侦察附近，看看是否还有需要战斗的地方。

sentences.en: There isn't.
sentences.zh: 没有了。

sentences.en: So Tacitus writes in kind of chilling terms, the silence of desolation reigned on all sides.
sentences.zh: 所以塔西佗用一种令人不寒而栗的措辞写道，荒凉的寂静笼罩着四方。

sentences.en: The hills were abandoned.
sentences.zh: 山丘被遗弃了。

sentences.en: Distant homesteads put to the torch.
sentences.zh: 远处的农舍被付之一炬。

sentences.en: Not a soul was to be seen by our scouts.
sentences.zh: 我们的侦察兵连一个人影都没看到。

sentences.en: And the estimate of casualties about 10,000.
sentences.zh: 伤亡估计约为一万人。

sentences.en: I mean, a real massacre again.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，又是一场真正的大屠杀。

sentences.en: And so Agricola assumes this is it.
sentences.zh: 所以阿古里科拉认为这就是结局了。

sentences.en: This is the great battle he's been looking for.
sentences.zh: 这就是他一直在寻找的那场伟大的战役。

sentences.en: He takes hostages.
sentences.zh: 他带走了人质。

sentences.en: He goes back south for the winter, but he leaves his men in situ, north of the Firth of
sentences.zh: 他南下过冬，但他让士兵们留在了原地，位于福斯湾以北，

sentences.en: Forth for the first time.
sentences.zh: 这是第一次。

sentences.en: They are commissioned to build more forts, to construct more roads, to absolutely nail down the occupation.
sentences.zh: 他们受命建造更多的堡垒，修建更多的道路，彻底巩固占领。

sentences.en: And at the foot of a glen beside the River Tay, a place that's now called Inchtut Hill, they build the most northerly legionary base ever constructed.
sentences.zh: 在泰河旁的一个峡谷脚下，现在被称为因奇图特山的地方，他们建造了有史以来最北端的军团基地。

sentences.en: You know, so large enough to host 5,000 men.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大到足以容纳5000人。

sentences.en: There's nothing really there to see now except for ridges because it's all covered over in grass.
sentences.zh: 现在那里除了山脊外真的没什么可看的了，因为全被草覆盖了。

sentences.en: But it is actually the best preserved legionary fortress anywhere to be seen in the Roman
sentences.zh: 但它实际上是罗马帝国任何地方都能看到的保存最完好的军团要塞。

sentences.en: Empire.
sentences.zh: 那是一个令人惊叹的地方，可以四处漫步。

sentences.en: It's an amazing place to go and wander around.
sentences.zh: 你真的能感觉到那里的幽灵。

sentences.en: You really feel the kind of the ghosts there.
sentences.zh: 它是作为永久占领军的总部而建造的。

sentences.en: It's built to be the headquarters of a permanent occupation force.
sentences.zh: 所以是一个了不起的地方。

sentences.en: So an amazing place.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在海上，罗马舰队正向北航行，目的是证明

sentences.en: Meanwhile, by sea, the Roman fleet is heading northwards and the aim is to demonstrate that
sentences.zh: 不列颠确实是一个岛屿。

sentences.en: Britain is indeed an island.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种感觉，你已经征服了陆地。

sentences.en: So there's a sense you've conquered the land.
sentences.zh: 现在你要征服海洋，海洋一直被罗马人视为超自然的一个维度。

sentences.en: Now you conquer the ocean, which has always been seen by the Romans as a dimension of the supernatural.
sentences.zh: 但现在阿古里科拉全力以赴了。

sentences.en: But now Agricola is all out.
sentences.zh: 所以他们向苏格兰北部进发。

sentences.en: So they head north of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了奥克尼群岛。

sentences.en: They see Orkney.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里登陆。

sentences.en: They land there.
sentences.zh: 他们征服了它。

sentences.en: They subdue it.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至瞥见了设得兰群岛，阿古里科拉说，不要去攻击那个。

sentences.en: They even glimpse Shetland, which Agricola said, don't go and attack that.
sentences.zh: 他在发回的报告中说，我们瞥见了图勒，终极图勒。

sentences.en: In his reports back, he says, we have glimpsed Thule, Ultima Thule.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，太神奇了。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, amazing.
sentences.zh: 然后他们完成了对喀里多尼亚的环航，证明了不列颠确实是一个岛屿。

sentences.en: They then complete their circumnavigation of Caledonia and they demonstrate that Britain is indeed an island.
sentences.zh: 而在罗马，你知道，这又有点像太空竞赛了。

sentences.en: And back in Rome, you know, this is kind of space race stuff again.
sentences.zh: 这就像登月一样。

sentences.en: This is moon landing stuff.
sentences.zh: 它受到的欢迎甚至比蒙斯格劳皮乌斯战役胜利的消息还要热烈。

sentences.en: It's greeted with even more enthusiasm than the news of the victory at Mons Grappius.
sentences.zh: 诗人们都在谈论它。

sentences.en: And poets are all over it.
sentences.zh: 世界的最远边界已经投降，退潮的洪水在周围咆哮。

sentences.en: The furthest limits of the world have surrendered around which the ebbing flood tide roars.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Great stuff.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们没说错。

sentences.en: Well, they're not wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些人边境在幼发拉底河或撒哈拉沙漠。

sentences.en: I mean, these are people whose frontier is on the Euphrates or in the Sahara.
sentences.zh: 能向北走这么远，是一项非凡的壮举。

sentences.en: To go as far as they've gone northwards is an extraordinary feat.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以阿古里科拉现在可以写信给图密善说，你知道，任务完成了。

sentences.en: So Agricola can now write to Domitian and say, you know, mission completed.
sentences.zh: 整个岛屿现在和平了。

sentences.en: The entire island is now peaceful.
sentences.zh: 现在安全了。

sentences.en: It's now secure.
sentences.zh: 现在被征服了。

sentences.en: It's now conquered.
sentences.zh: 于是图密善相信了他的话，把他召了回来。

sentences.en: And so Domitian takes him at his word and calls him back.
sentences.zh: 阿古里科拉回到了罗马。

sentences.en: And Agricola goes back to Rome.
sentences.zh: 他获得了显赫的荣誉。

sentences.en: He's given signal honours.
sentences.zh: 他在奥古斯都广场获得了一座雕像，那里所有的雕像都是城市历史上最伟大的英雄。

sentences.en: He's given a statue in the Forum of Augustus, where all the statues are of the greatest heroes from the city's history.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这是一项了不起的荣誉。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this is an amazing honour.
sentences.zh: 而在不列颠本身，岛屿征服的完成被纪念，

sentences.en: And in Britain itself, the completion of the conquest of the island is commemorated by the
sentences.zh: 在里奇伯勒建造了一座巨大的四面凯旋门，那里是奥卢斯·普劳提乌斯

sentences.en: construction of an enormous four-sided triumphal arch at Richborough, which is where Aulus Plautius
sentences.zh: 和他的军团最初登陆的地方，至今仍被视为通往不列颠的门户。

sentences.en: and his legions had originally landed and is still seen as the kind of the gateway to Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像孟买的印度门一样，英国人再次意识到这是一个先例。

sentences.en: So, rather like the gateway of India in Bombay, again, the British are conscious of this as kind of a precedent.
sentences.zh: 而写下《无界帝国》的维吉尔，你知道，看起来这是真的。

sentences.en: And Virgil, who'd written Empire Without Limits, Imperium, Sine Fine, you know, it looks like this is true.
sentences.zh: 它发生了。

sentences.en: It's happened.
sentences.zh: 罗马人做到了。

sentences.en: The Romans have done it.
sentences.zh: 但我说过因奇图特山，这座伟大的军团要塞，是保存最完好的。

sentences.en: But I said that Inchitut Hill, this great legionary fortress, is the best preserved.
sentences.zh: 那是因为它只存在了三年。

sentences.en: And that's because it only lasts for three years.
sentences.zh: 然后它就被废弃了。

sentences.en: And so, it's then abandoned.
sentences.zh: 它就像一座鬼城。

sentences.en: And it's like a kind of ghost town.
sentences.zh: 它就像一座鬼城。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that there is a massive crisis in the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 之所以会这样，是因为巴尔干地区正面临一场巨大的危机。

sentences.en: People called the Dacians, who are a very menacing military presence beyond the Danube, have crossed into the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 一群被称为达契亚人的部族，在多瑙河对岸构成了极具威胁的军事力量，他们已经越过边境进入了巴尔干地区。

sentences.en: Domitian needs to staunch this gap in the frontier.
sentences.zh: 图密善需要填补这一边境缺口。

sentences.en: So, he summons one of the four legions from Britain.
sentences.zh: 于是，他从不列颠调回了四个军团中的一个。

sentences.en: And Caledonia, you know, is a great trophy, but it's not as important as preserving the
sentences.zh: 虽然喀里多尼亚是一个伟大的战利品，但它远不如维护

sentences.en: Roman presence in the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 罗马在巴尔干地区的统治地位重要。

sentences.en: That might be fatal to the entire fabric of the empire.
sentences.zh: 如果处理不好，可能会对整个帝国的根基造成致命打击。

sentences.en: And so, Caledonia, the whole of Caledonia is abandoned.
sentences.zh: 因此，喀里多尼亚，整个喀里多尼亚被放弃了。

sentences.en: And if you go to the National Museum of Scotland, there's this incredible kind of tangle of metal
sentences.zh: 如果你去苏格兰国家博物馆，会看到一堆令人难以置信的金属

sentences.en: nails that the Romans buried to ensure that the locals wouldn't be able to get hold of it and melt it down and turn it into swords or spearheads or whatever.
sentences.zh: 钉子，那是罗马人埋下的，为的是确保当地人无法获取这些金属，将其熔化并铸造成剑、矛头或其他武器。

sentences.en: I mean, it's really amazing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真的很惊人。

sentences.en: Massive tribute to the scale of the occupation.
sentences.zh: 这充分证明了占领的规模之大。

sentences.en: And also, I'm sure, you know, the sense of disappointment that everybody who'd been involved in the conquest of Caledonia must have felt.
sentences.zh: 而且我敢肯定，所有参与征服喀里多尼亚的人，心中一定充满了失望。

sentences.en: So, Tacitus is, you know, I mean, he's absolutely merciless about this.
sentences.zh: 所以，塔西佗对此绝对是毫不留情。

sentences.en: He laments that Britain had no sooner been conquered than it had immediately been given up.
sentences.zh: 他哀叹不列颠刚被征服，就立刻被放弃了。

sentences.en: He blames Domitian for this.
sentences.zh: 他将此归咎于图密善。

sentences.en: He says that Domitian is jealous of Agricola.
sentences.zh: 他说图密善嫉妒阿古里科拉。

sentences.en: You know, he'd rather abandon Caledonia than allow Agricola to enjoy his glory.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他宁愿放弃喀里多尼亚，也不愿让阿古里科拉享受他的荣耀。

sentences.en: This is incredibly unfair.
sentences.zh: 这极其不公平。

sentences.en: Just because strategically, what is in Caledonia that would make you want to commit?
sentences.zh: 仅仅从战略上讲，喀里多尼亚有什么值得你投入那么多资源的地方吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I don't want to offend our Scottish listeners, but what is there in the first century AD that would mean you would want to commit so many military and financial resources?
sentences.zh: 我不想冒犯我们的苏格兰听众，但在公元一世纪，有什么理由让你愿意投入如此多的军事和财政资源呢？

sentences.en: When you have such pressing problems on the Danubian frontier or something which is much more important to you?
sentences.zh: 当你面对多瑙河边境那些更紧迫的问题，或者其他对你来说重要得多的事情时？

sentences.en: I mean, Domitian took the only possible decision, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，图密善做出了唯一可能的决定，不是吗？

sentences.en: Tacitus is a great hater.
sentences.zh: 塔西佗是个极其刻薄的人。

sentences.en: And of course, Dominic, as a historian yourself, that's not something that you would ever surrender to.
sentences.zh: 当然，多米尼克，作为一名历史学家，你绝不会屈服于这种观点。

sentences.en: I mean, you love everybody.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，你爱每一个人。

sentences.en: But Tacitus really hates Domitian and always thinking the worst of him and entirely interprets the withdrawal from Caledonia through the prism of Domitian's personal envy of Agricola.
sentences.zh: 但塔西佗真的很讨厌图密善，总是以最坏的恶意揣测他，并将放弃喀里多尼亚完全解读为图密善对阿古里科拉的个人嫉妒。

sentences.en: But he also interprets it in another way, and this comes to how Tacitus understands the Roman conquest of Britain and more generally the whole project of Roman imperialism.
sentences.zh: 但他还从另一个角度进行了诠释，这涉及塔西佗如何理解罗马对不列颠的征服，以及更广泛的罗马帝国主义计划。

sentences.en: Because as well as blaming Domitian for the abandonment of Caledonia, he also blames something profounder,
sentences.zh: 因为除了指责图密善放弃喀里多尼亚外，他还指责了一些更深层的东西，

sentences.en: which is his notion that the Romans themselves have been sapped by their very greatness, that they've become soft, that they've become flabby.
sentences.zh: 那就是他认为罗马人本身已经被他们自身的伟大所削弱，他们变得软弱，变得臃肿。

sentences.en: And this is why he gives this speech to Calgarchus.
sentences.zh: 这就是他让卡尔加库斯发表那番演讲的原因。

sentences.en: It's why he admires the Caledonians, actually, for the same reason that most Romans despise them, for their very lack of civilization,
sentences.zh: 这也是他钦佩喀里多尼亚人的原因，实际上，这正是大多数罗马人鄙视他们的原因，因为他们缺乏文明，

sentences.en: because this has prevented them from going soft.
sentences.zh: 因为这使他们没有变得软弱。

sentences.en: You know, they remain hard men.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们依然是硬汉。

sentences.en: That's what Caledonians are.
sentences.zh: 这就是喀里多尼亚人。

sentences.en: And this reminds Tacitus very clearly of the traditional Roman values that he is a huge admirer of and which he feels have been loSt.
sentences.zh: 这让塔西佗非常清晰地想起了他所崇尚的传统罗马价值观，而他觉得这些价值观已经丧失了。

sentences.en: And when he describes how Tacitus sponsors the civilizing of the Britons down in the lowlands,
sentences.zh: 当他描述塔西佗如何资助低地不列颠人的文明化进程时，

sentences.en: he sees this as essentially being the same process of corruption that has affected the Romans in the capital and across the heartlands of the empire.
sentences.zh: 他认为这本质上与腐蚀罗马首都及帝国腹地民众的过程是一样的。

sentences.en: So the dissipating effects of luxury, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，这是奢靡带来的消解作用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, again, there's a very, very famous passage where he describes this, you know, the process of wearing togas and having central heating and all that.
sentences.zh: 所以，又有一段非常、非常著名的段落描述了这一点，你知道，穿托加长袍、使用中央供暖等等的过程。

sentences.en: So he writes, so the population was gradually led into the demoralizing temptations of arcades, baths and sumptuous banquets.
sentences.zh: 他写道，民众逐渐被引入了游廊、浴场和豪华宴会带来的堕落诱惑中。

sentences.en: The unsuspecting Britons spoke of such novelties as civilization when, in fact, they were only a feature of their enslavement.
sentences.zh: 毫无戒心的不列颠人将这些新奇事物称为文明，而实际上，它们只是他们被奴役的特征。

sentences.en: And this essentially is the wilderness of which Calgarcus is talking.
sentences.zh: 这本质上就是卡尔加库斯所谈论的荒野。

sentences.en: It's not just the idea of, you know, a battlefield covered in bodies, cut to pieces by Roman swords.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是指战场上尸横遍野、被罗马剑刃砍成碎片的景象。

sentences.en: It's also this idea that everything that makes the Britons hardy and tough is being corroded and destroyed by what the Romans are bringing in to the island.
sentences.zh: 这也是指那些让不列颠人坚韧不拔的特质，正被罗马人带入岛屿的东西所腐蚀和摧毁。

sentences.en: And so this is why Tacitus is suspicious of empire.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么塔西佗对帝国持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: It's not for reasons, I think, that we would recognize today.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这并不是因为我们今天所认知的那些原因。

sentences.en: So, you know, if people are opposed to imperialism, it's not because empires have brought the good life to distant reaches of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果人们反对帝国主义，那并不是因为帝国给世界遥远的角落带来了美好生活。

sentences.en: It's because empire is seen as being murderous in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 而是因为帝国本身就被视为是杀戮性的。

sentences.en: But Tacitus is not lamenting that, you know, he's not condemning the Roman Empire for the reasons that we might.
sentences.zh: 但塔西佗并不是在哀叹，他并不是因为我们可能会想到的那些原因而谴责罗马帝国。

sentences.en: So the 40,000 killed in Boudicca's last battle, the 10,000 killed at Mons Graupius, the maybe 250,000, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，布狄卡最后一场战役中死去的四万人，蒙斯格劳皮乌斯战役中死的一万人，可能还有二十五万人，你知道，

sentences.en: this is the upper limit of David Mattingly's estimate of how many are killed over the 40 years that we've been covering in this series, probably an equal number enslaved.
sentences.zh: 这是大卫·马廷利估计的我们在本系列节目中涵盖的四十年间死亡人数的上限，可能还有同样数量的人被奴役。

sentences.en: And if you think that probably the population of Britain in this period has been estimated at about 2 million, I mean,
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到这一时期不列颠的人口估计约为两百万，我的意思是，

sentences.en: that's a quarter of people either killed or enslaved in this period.
sentences.zh: 这相当于这一时期四分之一的人口要么被杀，要么被奴役。

sentences.en: I mean, that is, to us, a terrifying record of conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，这是一份令人恐惧的征服记录。

sentences.en: And yet no Roman, including Tacitus, ever expresses regret for that.
sentences.zh: 然而，没有一个罗马人，包括塔西佗，对此表示过遗憾。

sentences.en: I mean, quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反。

sentences.en: They celebrate it.
sentences.zh: 他们为此庆祝。

sentences.en: They're building massive triumphal arches about it.
sentences.zh: 他们为此建造了巨大的凯旋门。

sentences.en: You said that Tacitus' reasons for criticizing the empire are not ones we would recognize, but they are ones that people would have recognized in the 18th or 19th centuries,
sentences.zh: 你说塔西佗批评帝国的原因不是我们所能认知的，但这些原因在十八或十九世纪，

sentences.en: during the time of the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 在大英帝国时期，人们是能够认知的。

sentences.en: That empire brings wealth, corruption, that you actually lose the very virtues that made you great by achieving greatness, that you become Warren Hastings, or you become so rich,
sentences.zh: 帝国带来了财富和腐败，你实际上因为成就了伟大而失去了使你伟大的美德，你变成了沃伦·黑斯廷斯，或者你变得如此富有，

sentences.en: you're no longer like a big game hunter on the veld or something.
sentences.zh: 以至于你不再像草原上的大型猎手之类的人了。

sentences.en: All of that kind.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: That's very familiar, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很熟悉，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's in all empires.
sentences.zh: 所有帝国都是如此。

sentences.en: The fear that empire brings a kind of moral corruption because you're too rich and successful.
sentences.zh: 担心帝国因为过于富有和成功而带来某种道德腐败。

sentences.en: I think that there is a definite Tacitian influence on this.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中绝对有塔西佗的影响。

sentences.en: Every British imperial administrator would have been familiar with the Agricola, but there's an even more sinister manifestation of this,
sentences.zh: 每一位英国帝国行政官都会熟悉《阿古里科拉传》，但还有一种更险恶的表现形式，

sentences.en: which is that Tacitus also writes a book about the Germans, who, of course, do not get conquered.
sentences.zh: 那就是塔西佗还写了一本关于德国人的书，当然，他们没有被征服。

sentences.en: They have held the Romans off, unlike the Britons.
sentences.zh: 与不列颠人不同，他们抵挡住了罗马人。

sentences.en: And in this book, Tacitus pursues the same theme, that the Germans are heroic, noble, they have resisted the sapping effects of civilization,
sentences.zh: 在这本书中，塔西佗延续了同样的主题，即德国人是英雄、高贵的，他们抵御了文明的削弱作用，

sentences.en: and it's this that in the long run will enable them to overcome the Romans.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，正是这一点使他们能够战胜罗马人。

sentences.en: And this is hugely influential on the way that the Nazis understand the patterns of history and the sapping effects of empire.
sentences.zh: 这对纳粹理解历史模式和帝国的削弱作用产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: So the thing that's fascinating, I think, about Roman history, or I mean, there's so much that's fascinating about Roman history,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，关于罗马历史最迷人的地方，或者说，罗马历史有太多迷人的地方，

sentences.en: one of the sources of fascination is that it is so influential on how subsequent generations in more recent European history come to see the past and therefore the future.
sentences.zh: 其中一个吸引力来源是它对后来欧洲历史中几代人如何看待过去，进而看待未来产生了如此深远的影响。

sentences.en: So much to think about here.
sentences.zh: 这里有太多值得思考的地方。

sentences.en: And actually, I think, let's do a bonus episode, maybe next week, for our Restless History Club members, exploring these issues about Roman imperialism,
sentences.zh: 实际上，我想，我们下周可以为我们的“不安分历史俱乐部”成员制作一期特别节目，探讨这些关于罗马帝国主义的问题，

sentences.en: and how it has affected the way that subsequent empires have thought about their own project.
sentences.zh: 以及它如何影响了后续帝国对自身计划的思考。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, you've got loads to say about it.
sentences.zh: 因为，你对此有很多话要说。

sentences.en: That's a great idea, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 这是个好主意，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, it's actually your idea.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上这是你的主意。

sentences.en: That's right, it's a great idea.
sentences.zh: 没错，这是个好主意。

sentences.en: I'm not going to take any credit for it.
sentences.zh: 我不会为此居功。

sentences.en: But, Tom, just to finish up for our regular listeners, so this brings to an end our little series about the making of Roman Britain.
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，为了给我们的常规听众做一个总结，这结束了我们关于罗马不列颠形成的小系列节目。

sentences.en: So just to throw ahead, with the end of Agricola's mission and the withdrawal to what becomes the line of Hadrian's Wall, would it be fair to say, I know this is a ridiculous,
sentences.zh: 所以展望未来，随着阿古里科拉使命的结束和撤退到后来成为哈德良长城防线的地方，如果说，我知道这是一种荒谬的、

sentences.en: oversimplistic generalisation, that to some extent the story is now over for the next 300 years.
sentences.zh: 过于简单的概括，在某种程度上，未来三百年的故事现在已经结束了，这样说公平吗？

sentences.en: Of course, things happen in Britain.
sentences.zh: 当然，不列颠还会发生一些事情。

sentences.en: There are mutinies or there are uprisings or whatever.
sentences.zh: 会有兵变或起义之类的。

sentences.en: But by and large, the story is now settled until, what, the beginning of the 5th century.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，故事在五世纪初之前已经定型了。

sentences.en: Would that be fair?
sentences.zh: 这样说公平吗？

sentences.en: Well, we're very lucky that we have as many sources as we do for this period.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们很幸运，这一时期有这么多史料。

sentences.en: And it's evident from throwaway lines or from archaeological evidence that there are actually great convulsions continue to happen.
sentences.zh: 从只言片语或考古证据中可以明显看出，实际上巨大的动荡仍在继续发生。

sentences.en: So the Ninth Legion, for instance, which has been repeatedly mauled throughout this story, it vanishes and that inspires the famous story, Eagle of the Ninth by Rosemary Sutcliffe.
sentences.zh: 比如第九军团，在这个故事中它多次遭受重创，最终消失了，这激发了罗斯玛丽·萨特克利夫那部著名小说《第九军团的鹰徽》的灵感。

sentences.en: And there's much debate as to what actually happened to the Ninth Legion.
sentences.zh: 关于第九军团到底发生了什么，有很多争论。

sentences.en: But the fact that we don't really know what happened to it is evidence of how many gaps in the record there are.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实不知道它发生了什么，这一事实证明了记录中有多少空白。

sentences.en: And over the course of the centuries that follow right the way up to the end of Roman Britain, Britain politically is very significant.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几个世纪里，一直到罗马不列颠结束，不列颠在政治上都非常重要。

sentences.en: It has about a tenth of the entire armed forces in the empire as a garrison.
sentences.zh: 它拥有帝国全部武装力量中约十分之一的驻军。

sentences.en: And in the long run, this means that it becomes what St. Jerome describes it in the 4th century as the womb of tyrants,
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，这意味着它成为了圣杰罗姆在四世纪所描述的“暴君的温床”，

sentences.en: by which he means it's a place that fosters would-be Caesars, who were endlessly kind of launching attempts to establish themselves as empires throughout the 3rd and 4th centuries.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是，这是一个培养潜在凯撒的地方，他们在三、四世纪不断地试图建立自己的帝国。

sentences.en: And actually, I don't think it brings the history of Roman Britain to an end.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我不认为这标志着罗马不列颠历史的终结。

sentences.en: So maybe a story to pursue in some later episode.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这是一个可以在以后的节目中继续探讨的故事。

sentences.en: Certainly, we should look at Hadrian's Wall.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们应该看看哈德良长城。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: And of course, Britain plays a part in the rise of Constantine the Great, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且当然，不列颠在君士坦丁大帝的崛起中发挥了作用，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And Helena, of course, comes from St. Helena.
sentences.zh: 而且海伦娜，当然，来自圣海伦娜。

sentences.en: His mother, of course, comes from Essex, as everyone knows.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲，当然，来自埃塞克斯，众所周知。

sentences.en: And Essex's girl.
sentences.zh: 埃塞克斯的姑娘。

sentences.en: And of course, the end of Roman Britain is a great story.
sentences.zh: 当然，罗马不列颠的终结也是一个伟大的故事。

sentences.en: So, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: We'll be back in Roman Britain for our club members with a discussion about Roman imperialism and its effect on later empires.
sentences.zh: 我们将回到罗马不列颠的话题，为我们的俱乐部成员讨论罗马帝国主义及其对后来帝国的影响。

sentences.en: But for now, Tom, a tour de force as always.
sentences.zh: 但现在，汤姆，一如既往的精彩表现。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: And we'll see you all next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
